info.title: Token Controller API
info.description: The versioned REST API of Token Controller. Everything the web app does goes through it. See docs.tokencontroller.com/reference/api.

get.summary:
What waits for the operators. Answers 404 to everyone else, so the web
app can ask it to decide whether to show the admin area.
The site assistant's questions of the last 90 days, newest first.

parameters.name: answered
parameters.description:
`false` lists only the questions the docs did not answer: each one is
a docs change to make.

get.summary: Every organization on the instance, newest first.

Everything about one customer: plan, members, support, feedback,
newsletter and notes.

post.summary: Keeps a note with a customer.

get.summary:
Feedback reports, newest first: every organization's for the operators,
the own organization's for a controller on an instance without operators.
One feedback report.

patch.summary:
Answers a report or marks it fixed. The sender gets a notice by mail
that links to the app.

get.summary: The newsletter list and every issue.

post.summary: Writes a draft. Nothing goes out until it is sent.

Sends a draft to every confirmed subscriber. The service sends it in
small batches over the next minutes.

409.description: Not a draft, or the newsletter is off

get.summary: Support conversations, the ones that need a person first.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
`new`, `answered`, `escalated` or `closed`. Without it, every
conversation that is not closed.

get.summary: One support conversation with every message.

post.summary:
Closes a conversation: nothing left to do. A new mail from the person
opens it again.

Answers a conversation by hand. The mail goes out within a minute, and
the conversation then waits for the person.

get.summary:
Your API tokens and CLI tokens, or every one in the organization for a
controller.

post.summary:
Create an API token. Anyone can create service and read tokens for
themselves; only a controller creates the organization token.

delete.summary: Revoke an API token or a CLI token: your own, or any as a controller.

post.summary:
Hand a service token over to another member, for example when its
creator leaves. Only future token entries follow. Its owner or a
controller can do this.
Ask the site assistant a question about Token Controller.
post.description:
Off unless `TC_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `TC_SITE_URL` are set. Answers come
from the docs only and are written by an AI model.

400.description: The question is empty or too long

429.description: Too many questions; try again later

503.description: The assistant cannot answer right now

get.summary: The organization's plan and members. Only on the hosted service.

404.description: Billing is off on this instance

post.summary:
Open Stripe Checkout for the Team plan. Controllers only. No trial: the
card is charged from day one.

404.description: Billing is off on this instance

post.summary:
Open Stripe's customer portal: switch between monthly and yearly,
cancel, change the card or the invoice address, see invoices.
Controllers only.

404.description: Billing is off on this instance

409.description: The organization never paid for the Team plan

post.summary:
Stripe's webhook. Answers 400 to anything not signed with the webhook
secret.

404.description: Billing is off on this instance

get.summary:
The clients: values of the `client` tag on projects, with their
projects. Cost per client is a filter on this tag.

post.summary: Send a message through the contact form. The answer comes by mail.

202.description: Received; the answer comes by mail

400.description: A field is missing or too long

get.summary:
The reports the signed-in person sent, newest first, with where each
stands.

post.summary: Sends a report from the feedback button. A signed-in person only.

get.summary: A report's screenshot, for its sender and the people who handle it.
Is the service up and can it reach its database?

post.summary: Take a mail from the mail worker.
post.description:
The body is the raw message (`message/rfc822`). The worker signs it; see
the mail decision record. A repeated id is accepted and ignored.

parameters.name: x-tc-message-id
parameters.description: The worker's id for this message

parameters.name: x-tc-mailbox
parameters.description: The mailbox it was sent to, such as `support`

parameters.name: x-tc-signature
parameters.description: Hex HMAC-SHA256 of the id, a newline and the body

post.summary:
OTLP logs: one model call per event, for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini
CLI and Cursor. Takes the organization token.

requestBody.description: An OTLP ExportLogsServiceRequest, as protobuf or JSON, optionally gzip-compressed

post.summary:
OTLP metrics: accepted and not counted, because the events already count
every model call. Takes the organization token.

requestBody.description: An OTLP ExportMetricsServiceRequest, as protobuf or JSON, optionally gzip-compressed

post.summary:
OTLP traces: one model call per chat span, for Copilot CLI. Takes the
organization token.

requestBody.description: An OTLP ExportTraceServiceRequest, as protobuf or JSON, optionally gzip-compressed

get.summary:
What an invite link is for, before the person signs in: the page fills
in the email and asks for a sign-in link.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The part after /i/ in the invite link

post.summary: The MCP endpoint. Send JSON-RPC messages with a read token or a session.

requestBody.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 message of the Model Context Protocol

get.summary: The signed-in person and their organization.

What a local tool needs to place token entries the way the service
does: the organization's rules and tag names, your own rules and tags,
and the projects with their ticket key patterns and repositories.

put.summary: Replace your own rules. They run after the organization's.

get.summary: Everyone in the organization.

post.summary:
Invite someone by email. They get a link that signs them in. Controllers
only.

409.description: Already a member, or the plan's member limit is reached

delete.summary:
Remove a member. They can no longer sign in; their past token entries
keep them as agent manager, and their service tokens wait for a new
owner. Controllers only.

409.description: The organization would have no controller

patch.summary: Change a member's name, role or tags. Controllers only.

409.description: The organization would have no controller

put.summary:
Assign a people manager the filters they read and approve, such as
`{"team": "web"}` and `{"client": "acme"}`. Replaces their filters.
Controllers only.

post.summary:
Send the invite mail again to someone who has not signed in yet.
Controllers only.
Confirm a newsletter sign-up with the token from the confirmation mail.

404.description: The link is unknown or expired, or the newsletter is off

post.summary:
Sign up for the newsletter. A confirmation mail goes out; nothing else is
sent until the link in it is used.

202.description: A confirmation mail is on its way, unless the address is already confirmed

post.summary: Unsubscribe with one click. The address is deleted from the list.
post.description:
Mail clients post here straight from the `List-Unsubscribe` header
(RFC 8058); the website's unsubscribe page posts here too.

get.summary: The organization's settings.

patch.summary: Change the organization's settings. Controllers only.

get.summary: The organization's rules and how they place token entries.

put.summary: Change the organization's rules. Controllers only.

get.summary: The organization's projects.

post.summary: Create a project. People managers and controllers.

409.description: The name or a repository is taken

delete.summary:
Archive a project. Its tickets and past token entries stay; its
repositories are freed for other projects. People managers and
controllers.

patch.summary: Change a project. People managers and controllers.

post.summary: Send a sign-in link to a member.
post.description:
Always answers 202, so nobody learns whether an address is a member. An
address that belongs to no organization gets a mail that says so.

202.description: A mail is on its way

429.description: Too many links for this address

get.summary: The page a sign-in link opens: a "Sign in" button that posts the link.

200.description: The page with the Sign in button

410.description: The link was used, has expired or never existed

post.summary: Use a sign-in link: the form on the link's page posts here.
post.description:
A browser gets its session cookie and goes to the web app. A local tool's
link only marks the link used; the tool collects its session with
`POST /sign-in/poll`.

200.description: A local tool is signed in

303.description: Signed in; on to the web app

410.description: The link was used, has expired or never existed

post.summary: Collect a local tool's session after the person used the link.

200.description: Signed in. The session token comes only once

202.description: The link was not used yet; ask again in a few seconds

410.description: The link expired, or the session was already collected

get.summary:
The ways to sign in besides the magic link, for the buttons on the
sign-in page. Empty on the open edition.

post.summary: Sign out: ends the session in the cookie or the bearer token.
Create an organization and send its first controller a sign-in link.
post.description:
The organization exists once the link is used. An address that is
already a member gets an ordinary sign-in link instead: one account
belongs to one organization.

202.description: A mail is on its way

400.description: Not an email address, or no name

429.description: Too many links for this address

get.summary: The state of every part status.tokencontroller.com shows.

Whether support inside the app is on, and where its answers go. Answers
404 when it is off, as on a self-hosted instance without support.

404.description: Support inside the app is off

post.summary:
Writes to support from inside the app. The answer comes by mail to the
member's address, like an answer to the contact form.

202.description: Received; the answer comes by mail

404.description: Support inside the app is off

get.summary: The tag map in force.

put.summary:
Change the tag map. A new version is kept; closed periods keep theirs.
Controllers only.

get.summary: The organization's tag names.

post.summary: Add a tag name, such as `team` or `client`. Controllers only.

delete.summary:
Remove a tag name. People, projects and tickets lose its values; token
entries keep theirs. Controllers only; not while the tag map uses it.

get.summary:
The values of one tag name on people, projects and tickets. For the
built-in names: the members' emails, the projects and the ticket keys.
The ticket systems the organization connected.

post.summary:
Connect a ticket system with an API token. Controllers only. The first
sync starts right away; whoever connects a ticket system answers for
that data flow.

400.description: The address or the token is not usable

delete.summary:
Disconnect a ticket system. Controllers only. Its tickets stay, and stop
syncing.

put.summary:
Set which projects of the ticket system feed which Token Controller
projects, replacing the earlier mapping. Controllers only. A project
without a ticket key pattern gets the one its tickets use, and a sync
starts right away.

400.description: A project is unknown or mapped twice

get.summary:
The projects the ticket system shows the token, to map. Controllers
only.

400.description: The ticket system refused the token or could not be read

post.summary:
Sync a ticket system now, without waiting for its 15 minutes. Controllers
only.

202.description: The sync starts within a minute

get.summary: The organization's tickets, by key.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of the key or the title.

post.summary: Create a ticket by hand, for work no ticket system knows. Any member.

409.description: A ticket with this key exists

get.summary: One ticket.

patch.summary:
Change a ticket. People managers and controllers; for tickets created by
hand, any member.

post.summary:
Report token entries. With a service token they arrive automatically,
submitted, and the token's creator is their agent manager. Signed in,
they are manual entries on your own token sheet, as drafts. Sending one
again with the same `session_id` or `local_id` updates it.

400.description: A token entry breaks the schema; nothing was stored

409.description: A token entry is in a closed period; post an adjustment instead

post.summary:
Import a CSV file of token entries onto your token sheet, as drafts.
Every row must be readable; otherwise nothing is saved.

400.description: A row cannot be read; nothing was saved

409.description: A row is in a closed period

post.summary:
Read a CSV file of token entries and show what it holds, with the
problem in each row that cannot be read. Saves nothing.

400.description: The file as a whole cannot be read

ApiToken.description: An API token as lists show it, without its secret.

needs_owner.description:
The person left the organization. A service token in this state
needs a new owner; its token entries show as an error until then.

person_id.description:
The person it belongs to: for a service token, the agent manager of
everything it reports.

shown_prefix.description: The start of the token, such as `tc_svc_3f9a`.

answer.description: The answer in a few plain sentences.

answered.description: Whether the docs answered the question.

links.description: Docs pages the answer comes from.

current_period_end.description:
When the current period ends: the next charge, or the end of the
Team plan if it was cancelled.

status.description: Stripe's subscription status, such as `active` or `past_due`.

Check.description: Whether one part of the service works.

CheckoutRequest.description: Start paying for the Team plan.

country.description:
The billing country as an ISO 3166 code, such as `AT`. Customers in
the EU pay in EUR, everyone else in USD.

Client.description: A client: a value of the `client` tag on projects.

Component.description: One part of the service, as status.tokencontroller.com lists them.

last_success_at.description: For a job: when it last succeeded.

ConnectionStatus.description: How a connection's last pull or sync went.

ContactMessage.description: A message through the contact form.

website.description: Left empty by people. Forms that fill it are taken to be robots.

Context.description:
Everything a local tool needs to place token entries the way the service
does.

oneOf.description:
The person's next token sheet. `null` until the close area reports
it.

rejected.description:
Token entries sent from this person's machines that the service
turned down. Empty until the close area reports them.

rules.description: The person's own rules, in order.
The organization's rules, in order; they run before the person's.

tag_names.description: The organization's tag names, built-in ones included.

tags.description: Tags the person's token entries inherit, such as `{"team": "web"}`.

ConversationSummary.description: A support conversation in a list.

oneOf.description: The contact's organization, when their address is a member's.

escalation_reason.description: Why it went to the operators.

suggested_answer.description: The answer the AI support answerer proposes; edit it before sending.

CostSource.description:
How a provider charges the organization. It decides what the close
reconciles against (docs: Account > Bills).

token.description: The token itself. Store it now; it is never shown again.

CreatedApiToken.description: A token just created: the only time its secret is shown.

CsvPreview.description: What a CSV file holds, before anything is saved.

problems.description: The rows that cannot, with what is wrong in each.

CustomerLink.description: The organization a contact belongs to, if they are a member.

CustomerMember.description: A member, with their newsletter status.

CustomerRecord.description: Everything we know about one customer.

members.description: Everyone who was ever a member, the ones who left last.

oneOf.description: Empty when the organization never started a checkout.

support.description: Conversations with its members' addresses, closed ones too.

CustomerSummary.description: An organization in the customer list.

members.description: Members who have not left, joined or invited.

open_feedback.description: Feedback reports from its members nobody answered yet.

open_support.description: Support conversations from its members that are not closed.

oneOf.description: Solo or the Team plan; empty when billing is off (self-hosted).

Diagnostics.description:
Sent with every report, and shown to the person before they send it.
Nothing else rides along: unknown fields are refused.

errors.description: The last error messages the app showed, at most 10.

page.description:
The page's path, such as `/reports/cost-sheet`. Anything after `?` or
`#` is dropped.

request_ids.description: The `x-request-id` of the last requests to the service, at most 10.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

message.description: What went wrong, in plain English.

ExternalProject.description: A project in a ticket system, to map onto a Token Controller project.

key.description:
What [`fetch_updated`] takes: the Jira Cloud project key (`KD`), the
Azure DevOps project ID, or the `GitHub` repository as `owner/name`.

HandOver.description:
Move a service token to another person, who becomes the agent manager
of its future token entries.

Health.description: The answer of the health endpoint.

edition.description: `open`, or the edition the Enterprise plan build reports.

InviteView.description: What an invite link shows before sign-in.

email.description: The address the invite went to; sign in with it.

Invited.description: A member who was just invited, and the link they got by mail.

invite_url.description: Opens sign-in with the email filled in; `tc connect` takes it too.

IssueText.description: A new issue, or a change to a draft. Fields left out stay as they are.

body.description: Plain text. Every mail adds the one-click unsubscribe link below it.

delivered.description: How many of them have it.

recipients.description: Subscribers it goes or went to; 0 for a draft.

LinkSent.description: The same answer whether or not the address belongs to anyone.

poll_token.description: For a local tool: pass it to `POST /sign-in/poll`.

LinkToken.description: The token in a sign-in link.

Mapping.description: One project of a ticket system mapped to a Token Controller project.

external.description:
The ticket system's project: the Jira project key, the Azure DevOps
project ID or the GitHub repository as `owner/name`, as
`GET /ticket-systems/{id}/projects` lists them.

external_name.description: Its name. Optional when mapping; the key stands in.

project.description: The Token Controller project, by name.

controller_notice.description:
For controllers only: a notice to show on every page, such as an
Enterprise plan renewal. `null` when there is none.

credential.description: `session` for a person, `read` for a read token.

MemberChange.description:
A change to a member. Fields left out stay as they are. Tags replace the
member's tags; only their future token entries follow.

MemberView.description: A member as the API shows them.

filters.description:
For a people manager: the filters they read and approve, such as
`{"team": "web"}` or `{"client": "acme"}`.

tags.description: Tags their new token entries inherit, such as `{"team": "web"}`.

links.description: Docs pages the answer links to.

sent_at.description: When our reply went out by mail; empty while it waits.

NewMessage.description: One model call of a token entry.

message_id.description: The agent harness's ID for this call, unique within the session.

model.description: The model of this call, when it differs from the token entry's.

reported_cost.description: The agent's own cost figure for this call, in US dollars.

request_id.description: The provider's request ID, when the agent harness knows it.

NewNote.description: A note to keep with a customer.

text.description:
Such as what a call was about, or their answer to "What was hard
this month?".

NewReport.description: A report from the feedback button.

oneOf.description: Off unless the person turned it on.

NewSplit.description: One share of a token entry with its own tags.

message_ids.description: A segment: the messages it holds. Exact.

share_percent.description: A share by hand, in percent.

project_id.description: Without it, the project whose ticket key pattern matches the key.

email.description:
For Jira Cloud: the email of the Atlassian account the token belongs
to. Jira Cloud signs in with both.

site.description:
The Jira Cloud site, such as `https://acme.atlassian.net`, the Azure
DevOps organization, such as `https://dev.azure.com/acme`, or
`https://api.github.com`.

token.description: An API token from the ticket system.

NewTokenEntry.description: One token entry as it arrives.

agent_harness.description: The product the agent ran on, such as `claude-code` or `support-desk`.

agent_name.description: A label for the agent, such as "review bot".

effort.description: The effort setting the agent ran with, such as `high`.

local_id.description:
The sender's own stable ID for this token entry, such as
`claude-code:<session id>`. Sending it again replaces the earlier one.

messages.description:
The session's model calls, when the agent knows them. With them, a
session seen by telemetry too is counted exactly once (ADR 0006).

model.description: The model that did the work.

placed_by.description: What placed it: a rule's name, `hand`, `classifier` or `none`.

provider.description:
Who charges for the model calls: `anthropic`, `openai`, `google`,
`aws_bedrock`, `gcp_vertex`, `azure_foundry`, `github`, `cursor` or
`other`. Without it, it follows from the model's name.

reported_cost.description:
The agent's own cost figure in US dollars. Without it the list value
is computed from the model and the price table.

session_id.description: Joins the token entry to telemetry.

signals.description: Facts about the session that hint at its tags.

speed.description: The speed setting the agent ran with, such as `fast`.

splits.description:
How the token entry is split, when it is: segments by message IDs
(exact) or shares by hand. Without splits it is one split.

summary.description: What the session did, from one line to a short report.

tags.description: Tags from the organization's list, one value per tag name.

ticket.description: A ticket key, such as `KD-214`. Wins over every rule.

NewsletterView.description: The newsletter list and its issues.

on.description:
Whether the newsletter can be sent (`TC_RESEND_API_KEY` and
`TC_NEWSLETTER_FROM` are set).

pending.description: Sign-ups waiting for their confirmation, deleted after 7 days.

Note.description: A note an operator kept about a customer.

approval.description: Whether people managers approve token entries before the close.

oneOf.description: How the provider charges; `null` until a controller picks one.

reporting_currency.description: The one currency the organization computes in, such as `EUR`.

sign_in_domains.description: Email domains magic-link sign-in is limited to; empty means any.

OrganizationChange.description: A change to the settings. Fields left out stay as they are.

OrganizationRules.description: The organization's rules and how they place token entries.

rules.description: In order. The default rules until a controller changes them.

several_keys.description:
What the "ticket key in prompts" rule does when prompts name several
tickets: `most_often`, `equal_split` or `first_named`.

summary_match.description:
Whether token entries no rule placed are matched to a ticket by
their summary.

OrganizationRulesChange.description: A change to the organization's rules. Fields left out stay as they are.

rules.description:
Replaces the whole list, in order. An empty list switches every rule
off.

OrganizationSummary.description: An organization's name and short name.

slug.description: Used in invite links, such as `kestrel` in `/i/kestrel-4f2a9c1e7b03`.

assistant_missed_7_days.description: Site assistant questions of the last 7 days the docs did not answer.

support_escalated.description: Support conversations that need a person.

PartState.description: The state of one part, in the words of status.tokencontroller.com.

rules.description: In order. They run after the organization's.

Plan.description: The hosted plans billing knows about.

session_token.description: Once, with `signed_in`: use it as `Authorization: Bearer`.

status.description: `waiting` until the person used the link, then `signed_in`.

PollRequest.description: Collect a local tool's session once its link was used.

Project.description: A project: a body of work made of tickets.

name.description: The value of the `project` tag, such as `storefront`.

repositories.description: Repositories whose sessions land on it, such as `kestrel/storefront`.

tags.description: Tags its token entries inherit, such as `{"client": "acme"}`.

ticket_key_pattern.description: A regular expression for its ticket keys, such as `^KD-\d+`.

ProjectChange.description:
A change to a project. Fields left out stay as they are. Changes reach
only future token entries.

page.description: The website page it was asked on, such as `/use-cases/agencies`.

QuestionView.description: A question asked to the site assistant on the website.

page.description: The website page it was asked on.

ReceivedReport.description: A report as the people who handle it see it.

Rejected.description: A token entry the service turned down.

local_id.description: The ID the machine gave it, such as `claude-code:<session id>`.

text.description: Plain text. It goes out by mail, signed "Token Controller support".

ReportChange.description: An answer to a report, or news on it. Fields left out stay as they are.

answer.description: Plain text the sender reads in the app.

fixed_in.description: The version the fix shipped in, such as `1.0.1`.

oneOf.description:
Without it, an answer makes the report `answered` and a version
makes it `fixed`.

ReportView.description: A report as its sender sees it.

fixed_in.description: The version the fix shipped in.

has_screenshot.description:
Fetch it from `/feedback/{id}/screenshot`. Screenshots are deleted
after 90 days.

Role.description: What a member can see and do.

RowProblem.description: What a preview shows per row.

Screenshot.description:
A screenshot the person saw, and blurred where they wanted, before
sending.

data.description: The image in base64, at most 3 MB decoded.

ServiceStatus.description: The answer of the status endpoint.

status.description: The worst state of any running part.

SignInProvider.description:
A way to sign in besides the magic link, such as the Enterprise plan's
OIDC.

label.description: The label on the sign-in button.

local_tool.description:
`true` for a local tool such as `tc connect`: the answer then carries
a poll token to collect the session with.

source.description: Where the sign-up came from, such as `/blog`.

SignUpRequest.description: Create an organization: the link signs in its first controller.

Signals.description: Facts about a session that hint at its tags.

ticket_keys.description:
Ticket keys found in prompts, the session title and the pull request
title. Only the keys, never the text.

Status.description: Where a report stands, as the person who sent it sees it.

StoredEntries.description: What storing gave: one result per token entry sent, in the same shape.

StoredEntryBody.description: A stored token entry as the API answers with it.

dropped_tags.description:
Tag names that were sent but are not on the organization's list, so
they were left out.

list_value.description: A decimal string such as `"0.03"`, or `null` for an unknown model.

StripeRedirect.description: A Stripe page to send the controller to.

Subscription.description: The Team plan subscription, as Stripe last told us.

SupportMessage.description: A message to support from inside the app.

SupportView.description: Support inside the app, as a signed-in member sees it.

answer_to.description: Where answers go: the member's own address.

TagMap.description: One version of the tag map (docs: Account > Tags and the tag map).

cost_center.description: The tag name that fills the cost center. Default `person`.

ladder.description:
The tag names that fill the cost object, most specific first. The
organization is the last rung and is not listed. Default `ticket`,
`project`.

version.description:
This version, counted from 1. The highest is in force; a closed
period keeps the version it closed with.

TagMapChange.description: A change to the tag map.

TagName.description: A tag name on the organization's list.

built_in.description: `person`, `ticket` and `project` are built in and cannot be removed.

TagValue.description: One value of a tag name and how many records carry it.

records.description: People, projects and tickets that carry it.

Ticket.description: A ticket: any unit of work.

assignee_id.description: The person it is assigned to. Being assignee costs nothing.

key.description: The value of the `ticket` tag, such as `KD-214`.

parent_id.description: The ticket it sits in, such as a story's epic.

tags.description: Tags its token entries inherit, beyond its project's.

TicketChange.description:
A change to a ticket. Fields left out stay as they are; `null` clears.
The title and description of a synced ticket come from its ticket system.

TicketSystem.description: The ticket systems tickets sync from.

TicketSystemView.description:
A connected ticket system, as the web app shows it. The token is never
sent back.

key_hint.description: The token's last characters, to tell tokens apart.

mappings.description: Which of its projects feed which Token Controller project.

site.description: The Jira Cloud site, the Azure DevOps organization or the GitHub API.

Token.description: The token from a confirm or unsubscribe link.

TokenCounts.description: Token counts by kind, as the OpenAPI document shows [`TokenCounts`].

TokenEntries.description: One token entry, or a list of them.
